expectations.text: Flags `ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN email TEXT NOT NULL;` as high risk, explicitly because it has no default and will fail against existing rows in the table
expectations.evidence: '[high] email NOT NULL — users — BLOCKS DEPLOYMENT ... will fail immediately with a not-null violation', explicitly because there is no DEFAULT and no preceding backfill.

expectations.text: Flags `CREATE INDEX idx_users_email ON users(email);` as a lock risk and explicitly names the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock type
expectations.evidence: ASSERTION IS DEFECTIVE. It requires naming ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, but CREATE INDEX takes a SHARE lock in Postgres. The response said SHARE, which is correct; the assertion is wrong.

expectations.text: Recommends `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` as the fix for the non-concurrent index
expectations.evidence: 'Use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_users_email ON users(email);' plus the caveat that it cannot run inside a transaction block.

expectations.text: Flags the migration for having no down/rollback as a reversibility gap
expectations.evidence: '[high] No down/rollback script exists at all' with the companion .down.sql it would want.

expectations.text: Recommends the safe two-step pattern for the email column (add nullable or with a default, backfill existing rows, then enforce NOT NULL) rather than only naming the problem
expectations.evidence: Gives the full add-nullable then backfill then SET NOT NULL sequence, including the NOT VALID check-constraint variant for large tables.

expectations.text: Does not flag `ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN nickname TEXT;` (nullable, no default) as a risk
expectations.evidence: nickname is never flagged as a risk; it appears only inside the suggested down script.
